key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence decay in metal halide perovskites from accelerated aging data, even for unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more informative stability screening of candidate perovskite materials, reducing experimental time and supporting materials-downselection for solar cell development.
method: Collected a diverse dataset of 167 perovskite compositions/crystallinities under heat and light stress.
Featurized 86k+ photoluminescence spectra using a physics-informed model.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL trajectories and identify stability descriptors.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on unseen materials and reported to generalize across material groups while outperforming baseline benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of accelerated-aging data, so extrapolation to new chemistries or stress conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
